1fa5a146ebd6.why: Explain resolving power of a telescope (optical_train beside lens_section lenses)

source.question: Explain resolving power of a telescope.

annotations.text: Resolving power describes the ability to distinguish two close objects as separate.
For a diffraction-limited circular aperture, the Rayleigh criterion gives θ_min = 1.22λ/D, where λ is wavelength and D is aperture diameter.
R = 1/θ_min = D/(1.22λ). A larger aperture reduces the minimum resolvable angle and improves resolving power.

source.question: Finding the focal length of a convex mirror with a convex lens and parallax

entities.role: lens real-image position and mirror centre of curvature
entities.label: I

entities.role: converging ray toward the lens image

annotations.text: First locate the lens’s real-image position by removing parallax.
Adjust the mirror until the returned image coincides with the object without parallax. The rays then strike normally and retrace their paths.
The lens-image position is the mirror’s centre of curvature: R = x_I − x_P. For a spherical convex mirror, f = R/2.

revealGroups.narrationCue: Locate the convex lens’s real image by removing parallax.
Place and adjust the convex mirror until the reflected image coincides with the object.
Measure from the mirror pole to the lens-image position, then use the spherical-mirror focal-length relation.
